self_support_reserve.note: Connecticut's 'darker shaded area' of the Schedule of Basic Child Support Obligations: if the noncustodial parent's own net weekly income (rounded to the nearest $10) falls at or below this threshold, that parent is a 'low-income obligor' and the schedule is looked up using their income ALONE (not combined income) -- the dollar amount shown is their full obligation directly, with no proration and no childcare/health insurance add-ons. Effective 2026-08-01, the commission replaced the old per-child-count thresholds ($280/wk-$480/wk) with a single flat self-support reserve of $362/week (125% of the 2024 federal poverty guideline for one person); the shaded portion of the schedule itself now ends at $470/week for every child count. Source: Regs. Conn. State Agencies 46b-215a-2c(e), CSguidelines.pdf preamble section (e)(4)(ii)-(iii).

deviation_note: Connecticut income figures in this calculator are WEEKLY net income, not monthly. Effective 2026-08-01, Connecticut's guidelines schedule was overhauled: income cap extended from $4,000/week to $6,000/week combined net income, self-support reserve raised to a flat $362/week, and a new three-parent worksheet was introduced (not modeled by this calculator). Above $6,000/week combined net income, the official guidelines describe a RANGE, not a single figure: the presumptive amount runs from the dollar figure at the $6,000 row up to that row's percentage applied to actual combined income (courts decide within that range case-by-case, General Statutes section 46b-84(d)); this calculator returns the upper end of that range (schedule.aboveCapPercentages), which is a presumptive ceiling, not the only correct answer above $6,000/week. This calculator models the standard (sole-custody) case only. It does not model Shared Physical Custody (Regs. Conn. State Agencies 46b-215a-1(23): when each parent has at least roughly equal time, the presumptive order equals the HIGHER-net-income parent's own calculated share, paid to the other parent, unadjusted for the specific time split), Split Custody (each parent primary for different children, calculated as an offset between two worksheets), or the new three-parent worksheet introduced 2026-08-01. Below $150/week combined net income (the schedule's lowest tabulated row), this calculator returns the $150-row amount rather than scaling down further -- the official guidelines direct courts to apply a 10%-of-obligor-income baseline formula at these very-low incomes, which this calculator does not yet implement; treat results below $150/week combined net income as approximate.
